title: Gratitude
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Gratitude is the thankful recognition of God’s grace, mercy, provision, faithfulness, and goodness. It turns the heart away from entitlement and teaches believers to remember what God has given.
summary: Gratitude is the thankful recognition of God’s grace, mercy, provision, faithfulness, and goodness. It turns the heart away from entitlement and teaches believers to remember what God has given.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the greatest gift of God and the deepest reason for gratitude. Through Him, believers receive salvation, forgiveness, adoption, hope, and every spiritual blessing.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Thankfulness is commanded because God’s people are prone to forget. Gratitude remembers who God is and what He has done. It blesses the Lord for forgiveness, mercy, provision, healing, and steadfast love.

Gratitude does not deny suffering. Scripture calls believers to give thanks in all circumstances, not because every circumstance is good, but because God remains faithful within them.

Thankfulness also guards the heart from entitlement, bitterness, envy, and complaint. It trains believers to see life as gift rather than something owed to them.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Ungratefulness can grow quietly even in people who know much doctrine. Pain, comparison, disappointment, or comfort can all blind the heart to mercy.

This doctrine helps believers remember grace. The thankful heart is not naïve; it is anchored in the goodness of God and the gift of Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice naming God’s mercies. Thank Him for salvation, daily provision, answered prayer, sustaining grace, and even the help He gives in hardship. Let gratitude shape your speech, prayers, relationships, and endurance.
